description: OrbitCare creará un software para monitorear la salud de astronautas en misiones largas. Detectaremos cambios físicos y mentales por radiación, microgravedad, aislamiento y estrés, con datos, alertas y recomendaciones. Buscamos personas en programación, diseño UX/UI, datos, salud, psicología, investigación o presentaciones. No necesitas ser experto: ¡únete a OrbitCare!
summary:
ORBITCARE is a space health monitoring system designed to protect astronauts during space missions. We developed an interactive platform that allows users to monitor important health indicators such as heart rate, blood pressure, oxygen levels, body temperature, sleep, stress, and other physiological conditions. It also provides information about risks related to microgravity, radiation, isolation, and changes in the human body.

Through simulated health data, visual monitoring, and an intelligent assistant, ORBITCARE helps identify potential health problems and provides general recommendations to support astronauts' well-being.

This project is important because astronaut safety is essential for the success of long-duration space missions. ORBITCARE aims to make health monitoring more accessible, helping protect astronauts and supporting future human exploration of space.
details:
What it does and how it works

OrbitCare is a health-monitoring web app for astronauts on long-duration missions, where radiation, isolation, altered gravity and a closed environment can cause bone and muscle loss, cardiovascular changes, vision problems and mental-health issues. Because crews are far from Earth, astronauts must detect many of these changes themselves.

The app has three parts. An interactive 3D rotating hologram of the human body links each body system (brain and vision, heart, oxygen, temperature, bones, muscle, sleep and stress, radiation) to what changes in space and how it is measured with wearable sensors. A Health Assistant takes the astronaut’s wearable readings (heart rate, blood pressure, SpO2, temperature, HRV, sleep and cumulative radiation dose) and compares them with reference ranges. It classifies each one as Normal, Attention or Alert and gives practical advice, recommending contact with the medical team when an alert appears. Finally, a monitoring dashboard shows live vital signs, risk summaries and calculators for bone loss and radiation dose.

Benefits and intended impact

OrbitCare helps astronauts spot problems early and act on them. The assistant is rule-based and runs entirely in the browser, so it works without internet, which matters on deep-space missions where communication is delayed. The same approach could support remote clinics and people far from medical care on Earth.

Tools and technologies

HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with the HTML5 Canvas 2D API for the animated Earth, the particle text and the 360° hologram, built with our own 3D projection and no external libraries. The site is hosted on Netlify. It is designed for wearable data such as smartwatch heart rate and ECG, pulse oximetry, actigraphy, bioelectrical impedance and personal dosimeters; the readings in this prototype are simulated. We used Claude (an AI assistant by Anthropic) to help write and refine the code, and our research drew on NASA and medical sources listed in the project.

Creativity

We combined an immersive space-themed interface with an educational hologram and a conversational assistant, so astronauts can both understand and monitor their health in one place.

Factors we considered

Autonomy under communication delays, clear alerts and simple language under stress, the fact that normal ranges differ between individuals (for example HRV), and responsible limits: the assistant gives general guidance, not a medical diagnosis. The reference ranges come from published sources and would need validation by medical experts before real use.
